summary: The Maldives grants a free 30-day tourist visa on arrival to every nationality except Israeli passport holders, who are barred from entry, provided you have a confirmed hotel booking, sufficient funds and an onward ticket. Every traveler must also submit the free Imuga Traveller Declaration online within 96 hours before arrival, and the stay can be extended in-country through the Imuga portal.

passportValidity.text: Your passport (or travel document) must be machine-readable and valid for at least 1 month on arrival, according to Maldives Immigration; the UK Foreign Office gives the same 1-month rule. Canada's travel advice asks for 6 months from your date of entry, so check with your airline.

conflict.name: Government of Canada — Maldives travel advice (entry and exit requirements)
conflict.states: at least 6 months from your date of entry

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required only if you arrive from, or transited through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not among the entry requirements that Maldives Immigration lists for tourists.

onwardTicket.text: A confirmed onward or return ticket is one of the conditions of the visa on arrival — airlines and immigration officers check it.

proofOfFunds.text: You must show sufficient funds to cover your stay, together with confirmed return tickets and a prepaid confirmed booking at a registered facility (or a sponsorship approved by Maldives Immigration). Maldives Immigration does not publish a minimum amount.

declarations.name: Imuga Traveller Declaration
declarations.submitWindow: Within 96 hours before arrival (and again before departure)
declarations.text: All travelers must submit the free Imuga Traveller Declaration online within 96 hours before both arrival and departure. Keep the QR code on your phone or printed. It is checked at check-in and at the border.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to bring in anything deemed contrary to Islam, including idols for worship, bibles, pork and pork products, and alcohol.
Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to export tortoise shell and coral.
Australia's Smartraveller says it is illegal to import pornography, alcohol or pork products, though alcohol and pork may be consumed on resort islands.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says major credit cards are accepted at resorts and hotels, US dollars can be exchanged at the airport, banks and hotels, and ATMs that accept some foreign cards are found only in Malé and the more populated non-resort islands.

safety.text: Crime is low on the resort islands, but petty theft happens — do not leave things unattended on the beach or in unlocked rooms. Outside the resorts there is gang-related violence, including knife crime, mainly in Malé and Hulhumalé; avoid empty roads on foot after dark. Strong tidal currents can drag swimmers away from the shore and cause drownings, so ask resort staff where it is safe to swim.

source.name: UK FCDO — Maldives travel advice: safety and security

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit the Maldives. The CIA World Factbook describes a dry northeast monsoon from November to March and a rainy southwest monsoon from June to August; Canada's travel advice instead says the rainy season runs from November to April in the northeast and from May to October in the southwest.

idp.text: Maldives is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Maldives is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Maldives yet.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says alcoholic drinks are available only on resort islands and you should not take any out of your resort: you can be arrested and deported for possessing or drinking alcohol, or being intoxicated, outside resorts and on inhabited islands. Importing alcohol is illegal.

Canada's travel advice says to dress conservatively, especially outside major cities and coastal resorts, and notes that publicly observing any religion other than Islam is illegal. The UK Foreign Office says that during Ramadan you should not eat, drink or smoke in public in the daytime outside holiday resorts.

The Imuga Traveller Declaration is free at imuga.immigration.gov.mv and must be submitted within 96 hours before your flight — for both arrival and departure. Ignore third-party sites that charge for it.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for the Maldives?
faq.answer: No advance visa for any passport that is admitted. Every nationality except Israel receives a free 30-day tourist visa on arrival — Israeli passport holders are barred from entry — provided you have a confirmed accommodation booking, means to cover your stay, an onward or return ticket and a submitted Imuga declaration.

faq.question: What is the Imuga Traveller Declaration?
faq.answer: Imuga is the Maldives' online traveler declaration, mandatory for all arrivals and departures. Submit it free at imuga.immigration.gov.mv within 96 hours before each flight and keep the QR code ready for check-in and immigration.

faq.question: Can I stay in the Maldives longer than 30 days?
faq.answer: Yes. The free 30-day visa on arrival can be extended in-country by applying through the IMUGA portal before your first 30 days expire. Your passport and accommodation details are filled in automatically (you can update your hotel if you have moved) and you upload a recent photo; Immigration expects to decide applications within 48 hours. It does not publish the maximum length of an extension or the fee.

faq.question: Can I bring alcohol into the Maldives?
faq.answer: No. Canada's travel advice says importing alcohol is illegal, and the UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to bring in alcohol. Alcohol is available only on resort islands; you can be arrested and deported for possessing or drinking it outside resorts.

faq.question: Do I need to change money into rufiyaa?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says the currency is the rufiyaa (MVR), that major credit cards are accepted at resorts and hotels, and that US dollars can be exchanged at the airport, banks and hotels. ATMs are only in Malé and the more populated non-resort islands.
